# Minimizable Panel Scope

## How To Build

A MinimizablePanelScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A MinimizablePanelScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

An inset panel for long-running work that can be put out of the way while the work carries on, and brought back to see how it went.

### Shape

#### Description

An [InsetPanelScope](../inset-panel/index.md#inset-panel-scope) with a minimize button beside the close button in its header. Each use names its work, the command that opens it, and how its work is listed among the [RunningActivityScope](../../../scope/running-activity/index.md#running-activity-scope).

#### Minimizing

The minimize button, whose tooltip says the work keeps running, hides the panel without stopping anything: the work carries on out of sight, and the window beneath can be used again, as when an inset panel closes.
Opening another inset panel, such as a file's diff, while it is showing minimizes it rather than closing it. Several panels can be minimized at once.

#### Coming Back

A minimized panel comes back just as it was left, steps or results. While its work runs, its row among the [RunningActivityScope](../../../scope/running-activity/index.md#running-activity-scope) brings it back. At any time, its command brings back the minimized panel rather than opening another; each use says whether its command also starts its work again.

#### Closing

Only closing the panel, with its close button, the dimmed window around it, or <Escape>, stops its work, and forgets it: its command then opens a fresh panel.

content.content:
## Concept

### Pitch

A floating panel over the whole main window, for work that needs more room than a popup and shouldn't disturb what is beneath it.

### Shape

#### Description

The panel floats over everything in the window, the ribbon and sidebar included, inset 32 pixels from every edge of the window. It has rounded corners, a border, and a shadow, and whatever it holds fills it. The window behind it is dimmed, and nothing behind it takes the mouse while it is open. Only one panel is open at a time.

#### Animating

The panel comes in each time it opens and goes away each time it closes with the [RiseInAnimation](../../animations/rise-in/index.md#rise-in-animation): the panel is its surface, and the dimmed window around the panel is its dimming. Switching what the panel holds, such as opening a diff while the settings are open, swaps it in place.

#### Modal

While the panel is open, nothing beneath it can take focus or input; only the panel and what it holds can.
The mouse can't reach anything beneath: no clicks, scrolling, hovering, or tooltips, except that clicking the dimmed window closes the panel.
Focus moves into the panel when it opens and can't leave it. <Tab> and <Shift+Tab> cycle through what can be focused within the panel, going round from the last back to the first and the other way, rather than on to anything beneath. Anything that would move focus beneath while it is open, such as a task beneath finishing, sends focus back into the panel instead.
The main window's shortcuts that act on what is beneath do nothing while it is open: opening the palette with <Ctrl+P> (<Cmd+P> on macOS), and collapsing or expanding the ribbon with <Ctrl+F1> (<Cmd+F1> on macOS). Shortcuts that open something of their own, like the settings window, or quitting, still work.

#### Closing

The panel closes with a close or cancel button in what it holds, with <Escape>, or by clicking the dimmed window around it; clicking inside the panel never closes it. Once it closes, focus goes back to the chat input.

33:Clicking the spinner opens a small list beneath it of everything running, one row each, in the order above, each with a small spinner of its own. Clicking a row closes the list and reveals what it is, first switching to its project when it belongs to another:
35:- a task brings back the latest task's output, closing the previous tasks and any inset panel over it, and scrolls it to the end

A divergence analysis, a rescope search, or a run target doesn't ask, and quitting stops it. The message is titled "Quit while a task is running?" and says what is still running: the harness working on a prompt, piton build, or both, and, when it runs in more than one project, in how many projects. "Quit" exits, and "Keep Running" or <Escape> dismisses it. Asking to quit again while it is open doesn't open a second one, and an open palette closes first.
=== application/MainWindow.md
29:#### Escape
31:Pressing Esc closes whatever it dismisses, such as a completion menu, a popup, the palette, or an inset panel, and otherwise does what it does where the keyboard is. It never moves focus to the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope).
44:The application quits with Ctrl+Q (Cmd+Q on macOS), Quit in the [PaletteScope](../palette/index.md#palette-scope), or the window's close button. Any of them asks first while work is running, as the [RunningActivityScope](../running-activity/index.md#running-activity-scope) says.
68:A file's [DiffViewScope](../../ui/components/diff-view/index.md#diff-view-scope), opened from the [FileTreeScope](../../ui/components/file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope), opens in an [InsetPanelScope](../../ui/components/inset-panel/index.md#inset-panel-scope). It leaves the body's tabs alone: every file open in them stays open, unsaved changes and all. Opening another file's diff replaces the one in the panel, as does opening one while a new project is being set up. Opening the file from the diff closes the panel and opens the file, as the [OpenFileScope](../open-file/index.md#open-file-scope) says.
72:The ribbon's Analyze Divergence command opens the [DivergenceScope](../divergence/index.md#divergence-scope) as a [MinimizablePanelScope](../../ui/components/minimizable-panel/index.md#minimizable-panel-scope), to analyze, in place of whatever else is open there, or brings back one that was minimized.

Its Refactor sends its prompt to the prompt mode on the application's behalf, as the [PromptSendingScope](../prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says.

88:The ribbon's New Project command opens the [NewProjectScope](../new-project/index.md#new-project-scope) in an [InsetPanelScope](../../ui/components/inset-panel/index.md#inset-panel-scope), fresh each time, in place of any diff open there. content.text:
While the Run panel is running a target, it can no longer be closed. It can only be minimized or stopped. Once the target stops, the close button comes back.

- **Header:** while the target runs there's no close button, only Stop and Minimize.
- **Esc:** minimizes the panel, and the target keeps running.
- **Clicking the dimmed window around it:** also minimizes it rather than closing it. You didn't mention this one, but letting that click close the panel would break the "can't be closed" rule.
- **Once stopped or finished:** the close button, Esc and the click close it as before.

The change is in `src/run_view.rs` and `close_panel` in `src/main_window.rs`. I added all of the above to the existing Run panel test, and it passes.

**Which panels this covers:** only the Run panel while a target runs, because it's the only panel with a Stop button. Rescope, Divergence, and the Run panel's "finding how to run" step can still only be stopped by closing them. If they lost their close button while running, there would be no way to stop them. If you want them covered too, they'd each need a Stop button first.

**Tests:** 392 pass and 5 fail. Four are the same system-prompt template tests that were failing before. The fifth, `selected_answer_text_can_be_copied_or_attached`, is intermittent: it passed 10 of 10 runs both with and without this change.

**Spec:** the Minimizable Panel and Run Targets specs still say closing, including with Esc, stops the work. They'll need updating to match.

**My mistake last time:** I wrote the Ctrl+Shift+Up constraints to `1790706091-Prompt_11d9795306eb4fee.understanding.md` instead of the file your instructions named. This task's constraints are in the correct file, `1790706286-Prompt_e4ff2375a63bddb2.understanding.md`. I've left the misnamed file where it is.
